findings: Source 2604.16188v1 (sha256 491cb4b9...) defines R_cyc as the least n such that every k-edge-colouring of K_n contains H_j in colour j, through an embedding with some t such that (phi(t),...,phi(|H_j|-1),phi(0),...,phi(t-1)) is increasing. S_n^sc is the star of order n with centre 0. P_n^mon has edges {i,i+1}. Before Proposition 2.2 the source says any two stars of the same order are equivalent cyclically.

Conjecture 4.16: for any a >= 3 and b >= 4, R_cyc(S_a, P_b^mon) = 1 + (a-1)(b-2). The MathDB text has the same quantifiers and formula. Its phrase 'star with parameter a' is resolved by the source as order a (a vertices), which Table 11 and my own exhaustive checks confirm.
Lean Colouring := Sym2 (Fin n) -> Fin 2. Diagonal entries are never queried, because H is irreflexive and phi is injective, so they are harmless.
IsCyclicEmbedding := Injective and exists t, StrictMono (j => phi (t + j)), where Fin k addition is mod k. That is exactly the source's rotated sequence.
ContainsCyc maps each H-edge to c s(phi u, phi v) = i. Sym2 is unordered, so orientation is irrelevant.
In CycRamseyProp, code 0 is colour 1 and is used for H1 = startStar; code 1 is colour 2 and is used for H2 = monPath. The order of the arguments matches R_cyc(S_a, P_b^mon).

cycRamsey is defined by sInf, and the endpoint proves IsLeast, so the 0-of-empty-set degeneracy is excluded. IsLeast also exhibits colourings without either structure for every m < N, so ContainsCyc is not trivially true.
startStar is fromRel (u = 0 and v != 0). monPath is fromRel (u + 1 = v).

Centre irrelevance and the degree and clockwise-path shortcuts were checked against the literal definition, for every centre position, on 4350 random instances with n <= 7: 0 mismatches (logs/defcheck.log).

B_ordinary_mathematics.verdict: PASS (the theorem is true and the candidate proof is correct)
findings: I re-proved Theorem A independently. J and K are at most t+1 since t+1 <= N-1. The two non-neighbour runs, at offsets 1..J-1 and N-K+1..N-1, are disjoint iff J+K <= N+1, which holds because 2t+2 <= (t+1)(b-2)+2 for b >= 4; hence J+K <= t+2. The b-vertex sequence s-K(s), s, g(s), ..., g^{b-2}(s) has strictly increasing offsets and colour-2 consecutive pairs, so with no path its span is at least N. The span is also at most (t+2)+(b-3)(t+1) = N, so equality is forced, and J(g(s)) = t+1 because b-3 >= 1. The orbit from u = g(0) has K(u) = 1, and J(u + k(t+1)) = t+1 for every k; at k = b-2 the orbit reaches u-1 with J(u-1) >= 2, which contradicts u ~ u-1.
The lower bound (source Theorem 4.5, block colouring) re-checked, including the wrap pair (b-1, 0) and the case t = 0.

The star application holds: a vertex with a-1 colour-1 neighbours, listed clockwise from the centre, gives a cyclic S_a; otherwise every vertex has at most a-2 colour-1 neighbours and Theorem A applies with t = a-2.

Own exhaustive pure-Python backtracking (scripts/rcyc_search.py, logs/rcyc-grid.log) gives SAT at N-1 and UNSAT at N for (a,b) = (3,3..9), (4,3..6), (5,3..5), (6,3..4) and (7,4) at n = 12. That is 16 UNSAT and 17 SAT verdicts, all equal to Table 11. (7,4) at n = 13 and (8,4) at n = 14 and 15 timed out at the 140 s wall limit and give no verdict.

E_significance.reason: The full conjecture is a one-paragraph bridge from source results. The lower bound is source Theorem 4.5. For the upper bound, source Corollary 4.19 (via Theorem 4.18 and Proposition 1.5) applied with b' = b-1 >= 3 gives R_cyc(S_a, C_{b-1}^mon) <= 1 + (a-1)(b-2) = N, so any colouring of K_N with no colour-1 cyclic S_a has a colour-2 clockwise cycle x_1 < ... < x_{b-1}. Each of the N-(b-1) = (a-2)(b-2) remaining vertices y lies in a unique gap (x_i, x_{i+1}). If y is joined in colour 2 to x_i, then x_{i+1}, ..., x_{b-1}, x_1, ..., x_i, y is a colour-2 cyclic P_b; if it is joined to x_{i+1}, then y, x_{i+1}, ..., x_i is one. Otherwise x_i has colour-1 degree at least g_{i-1} + g_i, which must be at most a-2. Summing gives 2(a-2)(b-2) <= (b-1)(a-2), i.e. b <= 3, a contradiction. This is exactly the excluded pattern: a one-paragraph bridge from source lemmas plus an elementary count, as with precedents 369221, 374488 and 371637 and the same-paper sibling 374246. Theorem A, the candidate's Dirac-type reformulation, is equivalent to the Ramsey statement under t = a-2 and follows from the same bridge, so it adds no separate significance. Counter-consideration for root: the source authors still listed 4.16 as open on 12 Jul 2026 and the candidate missed Corollary 4.19, which shows the bridge was not noticed by them. The standard, however, judges the derivation, not whether anyone noticed it.
